# Deterministic journal id for the follow-up step of a payout

> [`deriveJournalId`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) turns a payout id and a step name (`sent` or `reversal`) into a fixed UUIDv5, so the follow-up ledger journal for a payout always gets the same id and a retry cannot post it twice.

_Part of [Payout journals in the ledger](ledger-posting-model.md)_

A payout first posts its own journal using the payout id itself as the journal id (done in [`run`](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/media/infra/ffmpeg.ts#L8), the `payouts.run-weekly` handler). After that, the `payouts.send` handler in [`PayoutJobs`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) has to post a second journal: either money sent, or a reversal. That second journal cannot reuse the payout id, because it is already taken. So [`deriveJournalId`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) builds a new id from the payout id plus the step name. It joins the two as `payoutId:step` and hashes that text with UUIDv5 inside a fixed namespace constant, `PAYOUT_NS`. UUIDv5 is a pure hash: same input, same output. The `sent` and `reversal` steps give two different ids for the same payout, and the same step always gives the same id. In `send`, a successful Stripe transfer posts the `sent` journal (`PAYOUT_CLEARING` → `PAYOUTS_SENT`). A definite failure posts the `reversal` journal (`PAYOUT_CLEARING` → the shop's account). If the job runs again, it computes the same id, so the ledger can recognise the journal as a duplicate instead of counting it twice. See [Payout journals in the ledger](ledger-posting-model.md) for the full money flow and [Retry versus reverse on send failure](send-failure-handling.md) for when each branch runs.

**Look at:** [`deriveJournalId` in payout.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout.jobs.ts#L98) · [`PAYOUT_NS` in payout.jobs.ts](../../../../packages/backend/libs/domains/payments/infra/payout.jobs.ts#L137)

## Pieces

- Fixed namespace UUID used for every payout follow-up journal id: `PAYOUT_NS` is a hard-coded UUID that scopes the UUIDv5 hashing, so these ids are stable and never collide with ids derived elsewhere.
- Function that builds the follow-up journal id from payout id and step: [`deriveJournalId`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) hashes `payoutId:step` with UUIDv5 under `PAYOUT_NS`, where the step is `sent` or `reversal`.

## What it touches

| Kind | Name | How |
|---|---|---|
| job | `payouts.send` | Calls [`deriveJournalId`](weekly-seller-payouts.md) for the `sent` journal after a successful transfer, and for the `reversal` journal after a definite failure. |

## Also relies on

- [Recording money in the ledger](recording-money-in-ledger.md): The derived id is passed as `journalId` to `LedgerService.post`, which posts the journal in the caller's transaction.

## Watch out

- Changing `PAYOUT_NS` would change every derived id, so a retry of an old payout could post a second journal under a new id. Treat it as permanent.
- The first payout journal uses the raw payout id, not [`deriveJournalId`](weekly-seller-payouts.md). Only the `sent` and `reversal` follow-ups are derived.
- Same id on a retry is only half the protection. The `PENDING` status check in the `update` call also makes the second run skip posting.
- The step type only allows `sent` and `reversal`; a new follow-up step needs a code change to that type.
